cands.bio: Democratic U.S. representative from the Inland Empire since 2015 and chair of the House Democratic Caucus. Former Redlands mayor (2010–2014) and councilmember (2006–2014). Earlier worked in the governor's Inland Empire regional office, as a credit union executive and as a business owner.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from Aguilar on data centers, ending homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, police pay and pensions, or school vouchers and teacher pay. We found no documented controversies. His Ballotpedia page shows he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys for 2020 through 2026, and the Ballotpedia page we received was cut off partway through the 2023 key votes.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.name: Stephanie M. Vargas

money.note: Individuals gave $721; PAC money $0; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Republican candidate for California's 33rd Congressional District in 2026. Chief Deputy City Clerk for the City of Colton and a local elections official. Describes herself as a wife, mother of three boys and a lifelong district resident. No elected office is documented.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the San Bernardino County Republican Party, Reform California, Redlands Tea Party Patriots, and several conservative voter guides (Ballotpedia list).
Campaign site lists endorsements from the California Republican Party, Congressman Ken Calvert and the California Rifle and Pistol Association (CRPA).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Vargas was born, where she grew up, or whether she ever moved to California. Her lifelong-resident claim comes only from her own campaign site. We found no record of elected office or of a vote on anything. Her campaign materials say little about data centers, development, land purchases by investors or foreign buyers, immigration or H-1B visas, abortion, or homestead property taxes. They mention lowering taxes and the cost of living only in general terms. We found no controversies, and no documented foreign ties. The Ballotpedia survey answers are short and general.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site calls her a "life-long resident of District 33" and a lifelong member of the community, which points to being raised in California; this is self-reported, and no birthplace or upbringing details were found.

score.why: Raised $721, under $50,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Chief Deputy City Clerk for the City of Colton and an elections official, who completed Master Municipal Clerk training at Cal State San Marcos. No elected office is documented.
qual.why: Senior local-government staff work with election administration and city procedures falls in the middle range. There is no legislative, budget-writing or prosecutorial record to raise the score.
